subcategory: utility-oriented selection of user-history records via contextual bandits (personalisation RAG)
task: Retrieval-augmented LLM personalisation (classification, regression and generation tasks)
problem: Personalisation RAG selects user records by semantic relevance, but relevance is an unreliable proxy for utility; record utilities are non-additive, so greedy top-k selection can introduce redundancy or conflicts.
architecture: PURPLE: a user-records encoder with token-level cross-attention to the query and a Transformer modelling inter-record dependencies outputs propensity scores; a Plackett-Luce model turns them into a distribution over ordered profiles; trained end-to-end with policy gradient using the frozen LLM's log-likelihood of the reference response as reward; at inference, top-K records are passed to the LLM (reranking a heuristic candidate pool).
retriever: BM25/Contriever candidate pool re-ranked by the learned PURPLE policy

datasets.name: LaMP
datasets.details: Citation, Movie, Rating, News, Scholar, Tweet tasks

key_results: With Llama-3-8B, LaMP Movie accuracy 49.6 vs 48.0 (ICR) and 47.2 (Contriever); Rating MAE 0.307 vs 0.312 (ICR).
With Phi-4-Mini, Citation accuracy 66.0 vs 64.6 for Contriever; Movie accuracy 38.6 vs 37.4 for REPLUG.
Removing inter-record dependency modelling causes the largest ablation drop (Citation accuracy 61.3 vs 66.2).
strengths: Directly optimises retrieval for downstream generation utility with an order-sensitive list model.
Consistent gains across three LLM sizes and nine tasks with three seeds; more efficient than LLM rerankers.

limitations.text: Requires reference personalised responses to compute the reward; real deployments mostly have implicit or noisy feedback.
Trained separately per task; transfer to unseen tasks or domains is not evaluated.
Absolute gains over the strongest baselines are often small (about 1 point).

title: Optimizing User Profiles via Contextual Bandits for Retrieval-Augmented LLM Personalization
